parsed.summary: The graph is mostly sound: the variable-gated routes and the t_key, t_way, t_code and t_ledger threads line up with the facts each node establishes. One route leaves a promised ending unsupported by its own entry, and several continuity gaps and weak forks remain.

findings.problem: The choice to flash the call is offered in the smugglers' store, but the ending depends on the hand lever, which only cm_light_study establishes in the lamp room. The ending itself 'establishes' hand_lever, and the store route never passes the lamp or the lever, so the writer has no way to make the flashing coherent.
findings.route_or_state: n_chamber -> cm_smug -> cm_smug_photo (knows_code=true) -> e_win_smugglers; hand_lever is never established on this path

findings.problem: d_hatch presupposes that Mira already knows about a floor hatch, but only d_locker_rope ('finds the floor hatch') establishes it. The dinghy and loft routes reach d_hatch with no hatch fact, and the hatch is not in the facts ledger at all.
findings.route_or_state: n_start -> d_boat1 -> d_dinghy or d_loft -> d_hatch

findings.problem: The gift for e_set_stair says the keeper 'never took a penny', but the truth and ledger say Ferris took the money for six winters and only never spent it. Prose following the gift would contradict truth_ferris_took_money.

cm_smug is written as 'Back in the store' but requires nothing. Readers who reached n_chamber via the keeper's door, the sea gate or the keeper's way have never been in the store, because store_seen comes only from tn_store.
findings.route_or_state: n_tunnel -> tn_keeper, tn_gate or tn_cut -> n_chamber -> c_n_chamber_2 -> cm_smug

findings.problem: e_win_promise has Mira writing a promise in the keeper's journal and winding the little lamp. Neither the journal in her hands nor a way to wind the lamp is established or required on this route. mira_carries_journal is established only in cm_leave.

Both safe options end in 'photograph the compass untouched' and show the same bait wire. Reaching first and then leaving it gives a weaker neutral ending than never reaching (e_neutral_honest versus e_win_hoard). The pocket choice is a signposted trap with an obvious right answer.

Almost every risky fork is signposted in its cost as a setback, and the patient or careful option always wins. The choices do not really differ and the lesson is always 'be gentle', so the many setback endings feel arbitrary for a 10-13 reader.

e_win_signal is typed as a success, but it only reveals that the spring was wound hours ago. The same discovery is already the gift of e_set_shaft, a setback, so the payoff is weaker than the label implies and nothing is resolved.
findings.route_or_state: cm_light -> cm_light_study -> c_cm_light_study_2 (and any knows_code=false reader, who has only this option)

findings.problem: Both options end with Mira soaked and frightened (tn_gate_dash and tn_gate_wait). The waiting option costs 'time' but does not avoid the soaking, so the only real difference is the ledger fact.

The two variable-gated conversation choices are mutually exclusive, so a reader sees only one. Both lead to the same ending, so there is no real fork, and e_win_keeper_found establishes lamp_code for readers who never learned it.

When has_key is true, cm_light_relight offers a single choice, so key-holders have no real fork there. Meanwhile the lamp-room payoff for key-holders is one-way into e_win_light_restored, which resolves neither Ferris nor Varley.

The endings section records gifts only for the setback endings. The neutral and success endings have no recorded gift, and e_win_ledger does not require crates_412 even though its event counts crates.
